> If Sanjo plays a card, is that not also a card I am playing?

It is a card that you the player is playing in the game, but for the
game itself, it's the minion playing the card, not you as the
controlling Methuselah. The only cards 'you' play are Master Cards.
Event Cards are simply put into play. Everything else are Minion
Cards, played by your minions.

> If so, doesn't this:

> http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/0981...

> "You can play Ventrue Investment as if Mata were a Ventrue anti, even
> if she is in torpor (as long as you have some other enabling ready
> Ventrue anti, of course). "
>
> mean that I can also play (through Sanjo) Terra Incognita as if Mata
> Hari were a Laibon even if she is not the one playing it?

The argument of that thread, and the eventual ruling, was in regards
to how a Metheselah plays master cards. Mata Hari's text doesn't
specify that she must be the enabling vampire for her sect/clan to be
seen as something else in regards to cards such as Ventrue Investment.

In the scenario, Mata Hari was in torpor, and thus not ready to be the
enabling vampire. But the player has a !Ventrue who is ready, so they
are allowed to play the card. For this card, her card text essentially
reads: "You may play cards that require !Ventrue as if she were !
Ventrue". Her text doesn't actually specify that she has to be the one
enabling you to play the card, and the card can treat her as !Ventrue
for when it is played.

In any case, a Metheselah cannot play Minion Cards. If they could,
then the "and she" in her card text would be redundent. Her card text
thus doesn't apply when your other minions play minion cards (such as
Terra Incognita), since it's neither you (as the Metheselah) or her
playing the card.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

A fair point. I was simply trying to draw from the explanations in the
rulebook, and differentiating between you the player and you the
Methuselah. It seems some context must be assumed depending on the
text on each card. Due to the 'or she' in Mata Hari's text, it seems
to indicate that the "You" preceeding it pertains to cards that only
Methuselah's could play, otherwise there would be no point in putting
in the 'or she'. Mainly this is to allow the playing of sect/clan
master cards. Without the 'You' in the text, her ability would
function much like Advanced Kemintiri, who is restricted to minion
cards that she plays. Without the 'or she' in the text, it could then
be argued that you could then have Sanjo play Terra Incognita, which
would then open the door for a whole slew of cards to be played in
conjuction with the ability (Follow the Alpha, Ensemble, Blood Feast,
etc.).

Hmm, thinking on it some more, it could be perhaps more easily viewed
if we consider the 'or she' as a restriction. Because of that text, it
requires her to be the one playing the minion card (since those are
the only cards that she could play), despite you the player being the
one to play the card. This would leave Master and Event cards as cards
'you' play, in regards to her text. Without a similar "or he" to
Agaitas' text, this leaves it open to all cards you the player play.

Maybe I need to think more on my ramblings before writing them
down. :)

Chris, Thrall of Arika

is more explicit because it's not a normal rush kind of card, there's
no way to block Follow the Alpha. It just automatically puts the
minion into combat with the opposing minion of the previous combat.

> > no way to block Follow the Alpha. It just automatically puts the
> > minion into combat with the opposing minion of the previous combat.
>
> > Chris, Thrall of Arika
>

> Mata can play it, but FtA (etc.) will no longer recognize her as !
> gangrel when the "as played window opens"

FtA will treat Mata Hari as !Gangrel for the purposes of 1) playing
the card and 2) resolving the card. The current timing window is
irrelevent. No other card will suddenly begin treating Mata Hari as a !
Gangrel as a result of her playing this card.

1) means that she can play the card as if she meets the requirements.
2) means that if the card resolves (i.e., isn't canceled), she'll
enter combat with the opposing minion (in the case of Follow the
Alpha).

If a card, as part of its resolution, is put in play, its while-in-
play effects are not considered part of the card's resolution, and
thus do not treat Mata Hari as a sect or clan other than her actual
sect or clan (Independent Ravnos by default).

-witness1
